title: Irrigation planner
summary: Design the watering system from the water source to each bed, check the flow, list the parts and produce a weather-adjusted watering schedule. No water-needs calculation and no water quality check.

features.title: Water sources and bucket test
features.story: As a beginner gardener, I want to record my water sources and measure their flow with a bucket test so that the irrigation design matches what my water supply can deliver.
acceptance: Water sources come from the points of interest on the map (well, mains tap, tank)
The app guides a bucket test: start a timer, stop when 10 L is full, flow rate (L/h) is calculated and saved
Each source can have several measurements; the latest is used
Flow rate can be edited by hand

The bucket test opens from the water point details ("Measure flow"), the irrigation flow check ("Measure again") and a roadmap task "Measure your well's flow" created the first time irrigation is planned; until it is done the flow check shows "Flow not measured yet"

tasks.title: Add water source and flow measurement tables
tasks.description: EF Core entities and migration for water sources (linked to a map point of interest) and flow measurements. Done when the migration applies and seed data loads locally.

tasks.title: Create water source API endpoints
tasks.description: CRUD endpoints for water sources and flow measurements, scoped to the user. Done when OpenAPI is updated and integration tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement flow rate calculation from bucket test
tasks.description: Calculate L/h from bucket volume and elapsed seconds, with validation for unrealistic values. Done with unit tests.

tasks.title: Build water source list and detail screen
tasks.description: SwiftUI screens listing water sources from map points of interest with their latest flow rate. Done when sources show and can be edited.

tasks.title: Build guided bucket test screen with timer
tasks.description: Step-by-step bucket test: choose volume, start/stop timer, show calculated flow and save. Done when a measurement is saved to the API.

tasks.title: Write bucket test instructions (PT/EN)

tasks.title: Roadmap rule: "Measure your well's flow" task
tasks.description: Create the measuring task the first time irrigation is planned for a source with no measurement. Done when the rule is unit tested.

tasks.title: Test water sources and bucket test on iPhone at the plot
tasks.description: Measure the real well/tap flow at the plot and confirm values are saved and shown correctly.

features.title: Method per bed
features.story: As a beginner gardener, I want the app to recommend an irrigation method for each bed so that I don't have to research drip lines versus sprinklers myself.
acceptance: Each bed gets a recommended method: drip line, individual drippers, soaker hose or micro-sprinklers
The recommendation uses the bed's crops, size and the local climate (drip is the default in dry climates)
The user can override the method per bed
The reason for the recommendation is shown

tasks.title: Add irrigation method rules to the knowledge base
tasks.description: Author rules mapping crop types, bed size and climate to irrigation methods, with dripper spacing per crop. Done when the rules load through the content pipeline.

tasks.title: Add irrigation method fields to the bed model
tasks.description: Store recommended method, chosen method and override flag per bed. Done when migration applies.

tasks.title: Implement method recommendation service
tasks.description: Rules-based service returning method, dripper spacing and a reason for a bed. Done with unit tests for typical Alentejo beds.

tasks.title: Expose method recommendation in the API

tasks.description: Show each bed's recommended method and reason, with a picker to override. Done when changes persist.

tasks.title: Test method recommendations on iPhone
tasks.description: Check recommendations make sense for the owner's beds and overrides persist.

features.title: System layout on map
features.story: As a beginner gardener, I want to see my irrigation system drawn on the map so that I know where to lay the main pipe, branches and drip lines.
acceptance: The main pipe runs from the chosen water source to the beds, using lengths from the map
Branch lines connect to each bed; drip lines run along each bed's rows
Pipe lengths are calculated and shown
The user can adjust the pipe route by moving points on the map
The layout is saved as part of the irrigation system model

tasks.title: Design irrigation system data model
tasks.description: Model for irrigation systems, sectors, pipe segments (PostGIS lines) and drip lines linked to beds. Done when migration applies.

tasks.title: Implement automatic layout generation

tasks.description: Endpoints to generate, read and update the layout, returning GeoJSON. Done when integration tests pass.

tasks.title: Draw irrigation layout on the map

tasks.title: Allow editing the pipe route on the map
tasks.description: Drag route points to adjust the pipe path; lengths update. Done when edits save to the API.

tasks.title: Test irrigation layout on iPhone at the plot
tasks.description: Walk the planned route at the plot and check lengths and layout are realistic.

features.title: Flow check and sectors
features.story: As a beginner gardener, I want the app to check if my water flow is enough and split the system into sectors if needed so that every bed gets water.
acceptance: Total flow demand is calculated from dripper count and flow per dripper
If demand exceeds the source's flow, beds are grouped into sectors that run one after another
The design always includes a filter, a pressure regulator and a backflow preventer
Sectors are shown on the map with different colours

tasks.title: Implement sector splitting algorithm

tasks.description: Always include filter, pressure regulator and backflow preventer in the system model. Done when they appear in the API response.

tasks.title: Show flow check result and sectors on iOS
tasks.description: Show demand vs available flow, a warning when exceeded, and colour sectors on the map. Done when sectors render.

tasks.title: Test flow check with real flow measurements

features.title: Parts list
features.story: As a beginner gardener, I want a parts list for my irrigation design so that I know what to buy, without having to track stock.
acceptance: Parts list includes pipe metres per diameter, drip line metres, drippers, fittings, filter, regulator and backflow preventer
Quantities come from the saved layout
The list is for information only (no inventory or prices tracked)
The list can be shared or copied as text

tasks.title: Add irrigation parts catalog to the knowledge base
tasks.description: Generic parts (pipes, fittings, drippers, filters) with units and typical usage rules, in PT and EN. Done when published.

tasks.title: Implement parts list calculation

Early-morning watering is recommended
Watering tasks are created automatically from the schedule
The user can adjust run times; adjustments are kept

Adjusts frequency advice to the weather (hot, rainy)

features.title: Mulching advice

acceptance: Connect at least one controller brand
